title: Divide Two Integers
hints: repeated single subtraction is too slow when the quotient is large - instead of subtracting the divisor once at a time, can you subtract a much bigger multiple of it at once?

any number can be built from powers of two - so the quotient can be built by testing, from the highest bit down, whether that power-of-two multiple of the divisor still fits within what's left of the dividend

work with absolute values throughout (track the sign of the answer separately), then for each bit position from high to low, check if (divisor << bit) fits in the remaining dividend - if it does, subtract it out and add (1 << bit) to the quotient

handle sign separately (result is negative if dividend and divisor have different signs), and handle the one overflow case explicitly: dividend = -2^31 and divisor = -1 would produce 2^31 which doesn't fit, so clamp it to 2^31 - 1
commonMistakes: using actual division or multiplication anywhere (even indirectly, like a language's built-in pow) when the problem explicitly disallows those operators
forgetting to special-case dividend = INT_MIN, divisor = -1, which is the one input that overflows a 32-bit signed result
truncating toward negative infinity (floor division) instead of toward zero for negative results, which gives an off-by-one wrong answer

content.problemStatement:
You're given two integers, `dividend` and `divisor`.

**Divide them without using multiplication, division, or the mod operator, and return the quotient truncated toward zero**, so the fractional part is discarded, not rounded.

If the mathematical result would overflow a signed 32-bit integer, clamp it to the nearest 32-bit signed boundary (2^31 - 1 or -2^31).
constraints: clamp the result to [-2^31, 2^31 - 1] if it would overflow
notes: dividend and divisor have different signs (result should truncate toward zero, not floor)
the overflow case: dividend = INT_MIN divided by -1

optimal.time: O(log^2 n) or O(32) per outer step, effectively O(log n) overall
optimal.pattern: bit manipulation (shift-and-subtract, doubling the divisor with left shifts each round)

bruteForce.approach: repeatedly subtract the divisor from the dividend, counting how many subtractions it takes until what's left is smaller than the divisor
bruteForce.time: O(dividend / divisor) - can be extremely slow, e.g. dividing INT_MAX by 1 takes about 2 billion subtractions
